summary: Sri Lankan 4-player partnership point-trick bidding game from the Jass family where Jack and Nine are top trumps in all suits.
rules_text: Four players in fixed partnerships opposite each other use 32 cards: 7,8,9,10,J,Q,K,A with rank J > 9 > A > 10 > K > Q > 8 > 7 and values 30,20,11,10,3,2,0,0 for 304 total points. Deal 4 cards each counter-clockwise. Auction: first bidder is dealer's right. Minimum 160, multiples of 10. Three passes in succession ends it; if all pass hand is void. Highest bidder hides one of his 4 as face-down trump indicator; its suit is trump but unknown to others. Deal 4 more to make 8 each. Second one-round auction from 250 upward can replace trump maker and indicator. Play 8 tricks counter-clockwise, must follow suit if able. Trump beats non-trump. Highest card of led suit or highest trump wins trick. Maker's team must reach its bid in card points.
